label: Every composite has a cause, other than itself, of its being: things diverse in…, from union
meaning: Derive the EXACT existing CompositeHasAUnitingCauseReading (every composite x has some c with c ≠ x and CausesIn c x esse), keeping Composite, CausesIn and esse as parameters, from five typed premises. Take a composite x. By two-distinct-components (q.11 a.1, sourced) it has components a ≠ b. By the uniting-cause principle (q.3 a.7 third proof, sourced) some c unites a and b into x. By uniter-causes-being (unattributed) CausesIn c x esse. By uniter-is-efficient (unattributed; supported by SCG I.18 n.4) c efficiently causes x in some respect r; if c were x, x would be an efficient cause of itself in r, contradicting STMT-NOTHING-IS-EFFICIENT-CAUSE-OF-ITSELF (q.2 a.3, sourced, and itself derived in AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-SECUNDA-VIA from two sourced priority premises). So c ≠ x. No premise contains the conclusion: distinctness is derived, not assumed, and STMT-COMPOSITE-UNITING-CAUSE-CONTROLS shows each premise is needed. All five premises remain open: three are sourced but undefended, and the two bridges uniter-is-efficient and uniter-causes-being are unattributed premises that SCG I.18 n.4 (Componens autem est causa efficiens compositi, with no present-time qualifier) supports and q.3 a.7 tertio and q.11 a.1 motivate, none stating them (Codex review on #983). The derivation does not establish that anything is composite, that the uniter is actual, outside or a nonpart of the composite, or that rival accounts of composition (brute composition, priority monism, composition as identity) are false: each is located at a premise it rejects, not refuted.
